note: Native proposal validation, accepted merge, and task completion remain separate gates. This receipt does not mark the backlog complete. The refresh pipeline pins inventory, dispositions, rights, catalog schema, coverage, ledger, and geography by SHA-256, audits rights, schema, and coverage, and publishes only outside the site. A failed audit leaves current.json unchanged. Site maintainers own that pipeline. The host supervisor owns process recovery. Credentials are refused before publish.

The same command run again exited 0 with action unchanged and the same snapshot id. That store was then removed. It is not site content.

node --experimental-strip-types scripts/worldwide/refresh.ts --self-test exited 0: 18 checks. Those checks cover a repeated publish, rights rejection, schema rejection, credential rejection, atomic rollback in both directions, refusal of an in-site store, and refusal to invent a rollback target. The credential-shaped fixture is assembled at runtime so the source text does not contain an assigned credential.

The pipeline does not fetch upstream datasets, does not rewrite scripts/worldwide/update.ts snapshots, and does not rebuild the browser catalog. It does not read config/worldwide_supervisor_host.json and does not start, stop, or restart the supervisor or watchdog.

A leftover .refresh.lock blocks the next publish until that file is removed. The pipeline does not steal a lock. A corrupt current pointer fails closed and is not replaced with an invented snapshot. The first successful publish has no previous.json until a later publish copies the old pointer.
